doc.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Shelly Manne, the Candolis and 1957 records
title: The Fabulous Bill Holman: the album's title, cover and Airegin
summary: How Shelly Manne's Decca deal produced his big-band album, his embarrassment at the title and cover, and doing a small-group tune like Airegin for big band.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I just want to briefly return to The Fabulous Bill Holman, the title of that album. I can‟t imagine that that was something that you chose, but perhaps you can set the record straight on that.

I don‟t know where – Shelly Manne was the producer on that, because a well known guy that had worked for Decca had called him and asked him to produce four jazz albums in L.A. We have to go back a little further, to a guy named Red Clyde, who was doing a lot of recording out here. I can‟t think of the name of the label, but he commissioned me to write an album of big-band music and was going to record it. So I got all the charts done, and I called Red and said, “Okay, Red. We‟re ready to go.” He said, “We‟re having a little bit of budget trouble. Can we put it off a little bit?” “Okay.” So we put it off and put it off. Finally it became apparent it wasn‟t going to happen. At this time, Shelly got this offer from the guy at Decca to do the four records, and he said, “Okay. Holman‟s big band is going to be one.” That was that. I‟m sure The Fabulous didn‟t come from him. I think it must have come from upstairs in the warrens of Decca and Corl Records. Then they got a professional photographer to make the album cover. That was a further intrigue, with a spacey look on my face. I‟m gazing into the future with a cigarette and my tenor and a scorepad. Really kind of embarrassing at the time. Plus, with that title, I hesitated before recommending it to people I knew.
But you were happy with the music?

Yeah. The music is kind of old-timey on that thing. I was bouncing back from Kenton‟s band, where nothing could be old-timey. I got a lot of this other stuff out of my system that I‟d been holding back all those years.

There was one other thing: Airegin. That caused a little comment, because it was a jazz tune that had been done by small groups and never by a big band. People looked around and saw that very few small-band records were making it to a big band. So that opened some guys‟ eyes as to possibilities.
Did you ever get any comments from Sonny [Rollins] about it?
No. In fact, I sent him a picture of – who was the baseball player?
Newk, yeah, a current picture of him. I sent it to Sonny. He wrote me back a letter. He didn‟t know who I was.
